text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Bahrain's Emir Sheikh Isa bin Sulman al-Khalifa says Manama is keen on boosting ties with Kuwait.
- Investment and real estate shares at the Kuwait Stock Exchange over-priced, investment firm official says.
- Real Estate Bank says mid-year net profit rose 1.2 percent to 3.54 million dinars ($11.6 million).
- Selective trade at the Kuwait Stock Exchange on Wednesday, trade value rises 14.5 percent to 25.3 million dianrs compared to Tuesday.
- Health Ministry bars state-run specialised hospitals from admitting foreign patients. Kuwait plans to impose a health insurance fee on its 1.25 million expatriates.
- The International Investor (TII) mid-year net profit amount to two million dinars for the first half of 1997.
- Kuwait Medical Association comes out in support of drugs ban on expatriates. Kuwait told state hospitals to stop disbursing 81 medicines for non-Kuwaitis in a bid to cut costs.
